title: Connettivi Testuali Avanzati
subtitle: Linking ideas like a fluent writer: contrast, cause, consequence, addition.
objectives: Use a range of connectors beyond the basic e, ma, perché
Choose connectors appropriate to formal written Italian
Structure a short argumentative paragraph with clear logical connectors

content.intro: Fluent written Italian relies on a richer set of connectors than everyday speech — signalling contrast, consequence, and addition precisely instead of stringing ideas together with e and ma.
content.explanation: These connectors are especially common in essays, articles, and formal writing/speech. Many pair naturally: da un lato... dall'altro (on one hand... on the other).

rules.heading: a) Contrast
rules.body: tuttavia, però, nonostante ciò, d'altra parte, al contrario, mentre — all stronger/more formal alternatives to ma.

rules.heading: b) Cause and consequence
rules.body: poiché, dato che, dal momento che (cause, more formal than perché); quindi, perciò, di conseguenza, pertanto (consequence, more formal than allora).

rules.heading: c) Addition and sequence
rules.body: inoltre, per di più, in aggiunta (addition); innanzitutto, in primo luogo, infine (sequencing an argument).

examples.it: Il progetto è ambizioso; tuttavia, i tempi sono realistici.
examples.en: The project is ambitious; however, the timeline is realistic.

examples.it: Dato che il traffico era intenso, siamo arrivati in ritardo.
examples.en: Since traffic was heavy, we arrived late.

examples.it: Il costo è aumentato; di conseguenza, abbiamo dovuto rivedere il budget.
examples.en: The cost increased; as a result, we had to revise the budget.

examples.it: Da un lato capisco le tue ragioni; dall'altro, non sono d'accordo.
examples.en: On one hand I understand your reasons; on the other, I don't agree.

commonMistakes.wrong: Perciò using it to introduce a cause (instead of a consequence)
commonMistakes.right: poiché/dato che for cause; perciò/quindi for consequence
commonMistakes.why: Cause and consequence connectors aren't interchangeable — mixing them reverses the logical relationship of the sentence.

commonMistakes.right: però/allora in casual speech; tuttavia/quindi in writing
commonMistakes.why: These heavier connectors read as formal/written register — using them constantly in casual speech can sound stilted.

items.prompt: ___ pioveva, siamo usciti lo stesso. (since/given that)
Ha lavorato molto; ___, ha ottenuto una promozione. (as a result)

summary: Formal connectors express cause (poiché, dato che), consequence (quindi, perciò), and contrast (tuttavia, d'altra parte) more precisely than e/ma/perché.
Cause and consequence connectors are not interchangeable — they mark opposite logical directions.
Heavier connectors belong mainly to written/formal register, not everyday conversation.
